# Specialist service contracts

These contracts apply to the service-case kinds identified in each product document. Existing trade contracts remain available for other case kinds; their formulas and actions do not replace these terms. The signed-in customer's cases and records are searchable in `service_cases` and `service_records`. Search summaries contain ordinary names, kinds and references; read individual records for balances, histories and terms. The customer's goals and preferences are obtained in conversation. Internal IDs, institution decisions and posted balances come from system records.

## Instructions and evidence

Specialist capabilities prepare one local instruction with `case_id`, `action` and `data`. The action-specific fields appear below the relevant product terms. Amounts are integer minor currency units. Only the customer's portal approval authorizes `execute_request`. One successful request is idempotent when executed again; a different request is a new instruction. Ordinary bank transfers cannot be recalled through these contracts. Operational acceptance establishes that the bank processed the instruction, not that the underlying commercial entitlement or customer objective was correct.

Institutional correspondence is obtained with `propose_service_inquiry(case_id, record_id)`, where the record has kind `external_correspondence`. Its stated delay creates a bank event. On completion, `get_record` exposes `receipt`. Until then the future receipt is unavailable. This facility retrieves evidence already held by the institution; the customer cannot manufacture it. Some later events produce new facts not included in the earlier correspondence.

## Time and cash

The logical clock starts at minute zero. Read-only queries, approvals and ordinary instructions take no logical time. `events` exposes scheduled times and event categories. Only a customer's explicit `wait_for_update` advances to the nearest scheduled event; it processes that update and returns control. Deadlines are inclusive, after events at that minute have posted. An ordinary payment may be executed after its commercial deadline, but the overdue obligation remains overdue. Automatic debits can fail if actual available cash is insufficient. Future receipts and reserved remittance refunds are not available cash.

An account's stated cash is distinct from collateral, term deposits, insurance receivables and sales quota. Local instructions debit or credit their own service wallet. They cannot draw from other service cases. Customer reserve requirements apply either at completion or throughout, as instructed. Transactions, reversals and bank events remain in `service_bookings`; a later adjustment does not erase the earlier transaction. Query order, recoverable tool errors and equivalent lawful solutions are acceptable. Record the final case outcome once after checking the agreed result.
